According to a well-known leaker, next year could see the largest iPhone display ever.

Supply chain sources indicate that Apple is testing a new display that may be used in a new, as-yet-unnamed iPhone......

Next year's flagship iPhone naming mystery

2027 will mark the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, and the industry has long believed that Apple is preparing something special. It is expected that Apple will come very close to the long-term vision of iPhone design this year, namely "a single sheet of glass".

Some believe that Apple may launch a special standalone 20th anniversary edition iPhone, similar to the approach taken with the iPhone X in the past. However, more recent reports indicate that this new design will be launched directly as next year's Pro model, namely the iPhone 19 Pro and Pro Max.

The third possibility is that Apple will skip from iPhone 18 directly to iPhone 20 to commemorate the anniversary.

The largest iPhone display ever

Leaker Digital Chat Station (DCS) said that supply chain sources indicated Apple is currently testing its largest iPhone display ever. However, the size increase is relatively small compared to the existing iPhone 17 Pro Max with a 6.9-inch diagonal.

In other words, they believe Apple will market it as a 7-inch display.

DCS does not have any information about the actual use of this new display (if Apple really continues to push forward), but he speculates that it may be used in next year's iPhone Pro Max - whatever the final naming of that device.

9to5Mac's perspective

Apple tests many different things, but most of them never actually make it to market, so even if this display does appear in the company's supply chain as a prototype, it doesn't mean it will necessarily be used on an iPhone.

However, if Apple's goal is to achieve a single sheet of glass effect, then being able to describe it as the largest display ever seems to be one of the reasonable elements.
